qt: to the Commission Danuše Nerudová (PPE) Subject:

The Czech Ministry of Culture now offers free admission to the permanent exhibitions of state museums and galleries on the first Sunday of every month. It also waived admission fees at state-owned castles and chateaux on two days in 2026 and promised the National Heritage Institute compensation for the lost revenue. While broadening access to culture is a welcome goal, privately run museums and galleries, which also contribute to preserving heritage and enrich the cultural offer, are excluded and receive no comparable support. They compete for some of the same visitors and could see lower attendance on free-entry days, without any compensation. 1.
Does the Commission consider that compensating state institutions for lost admission revenue may raise State aid concerns under Article 107(1) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union?
Does the Commission intend to assess how free-admission schemes in Member States affect private cultural institutions, and to promote models that allow them to take part on equal terms?
Could EU programmes such as Creative Europe support private museums and galleries in taking part in such schemes?
